Article Title: Narendra Modi becomes second PM to deliver 13th consecutive Independence Day speech
Article Text:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi addresses the nation during the 8oth Independence Day celebrations, at Red Fort in New Delhi. (PTI image)

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday delivered his 13th consecutive Independence Day speech from the ramparts of the Red Fort, becoming the second prime minister after Jawaharlal Nehru to achieve the milestone.PM Modi has addressed the nation from the Red Fort every Independence Day since taking office in 2014. His latest address came on India's 80th Independence Day.Also read: 80th Independence Day - A throwback at PM Modi's signature Red Fort turbans Nehru, India's first prime minister, holds the record for the longest uninterrupted run of Independence Day addresses, having delivered 17 consecutive speeches from 1947 to 1963.PM Modi surpassed former prime minister Indira Gandhi, who delivered 11 consecutive Independence Day speeches between 1966 and 1976.PM Modi hoisted the National Flag at the Red Fort before beginning his address, with the ceremony synchronised with a 21-gun salute by the ceremonial battery.
Article Summary: PM Modi has addressed the nation from the Red Fort every Independence Day since taking office in 2014. His latest address came on India's 80th Independence Day. PM Modi surpassed former prime minister Indira Gandhi, who delivered 11 consecutive Independence Day speeches between 1966 and 1976.

NEW DELHI: To mark India’s 80th Independence Day, Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived at the Red Fort on Saturday wearing a striking red tie-and-dye turban with a long trailing end, as he delivered his 13th consecutive Independence Day address from the historic ramparts.The turban featured intricate red, green and white patterns, reflecting styles associated with Rajasthani and Gujarati traditions. He paired it with a white kurta-pajama and a brown jacket, completing the look with three pocket squares in saffron, white and green—the colours of the national flag.For more than a decade, PM Modi’s Independence Day appearances at the Red Fort have featured a closely watched visual tradition: the turban. Since his first address as Prime Minister in 2014, he has chosen safas and turbans in a wide range of colours, patterns and regional styles, often bringing India’s rich textile heritage and craftsmanship into focus.From Rajasthan’s bandhej and leheriya to tricolour-inspired designs, his choice of headgear has evolved from year to year while retaining its traditional character. Here is a look back at the distinctive turbans that have become a recognisable feature of Modi’s Independence Day appearances.For the 79th Independence Day, Modi opted for an all-saffron safa, paired with a white kurta and churidar, a saffron bandhgala jacket and a tricolour stole.The saffron turban marked his 12th consecutive Independence Day address from the historic Red Fort.In 2024, Modi chose a leheriya-print turban featuring bold orange, dark green and yellow streaks, with a long, deeply pleated tail.Leheriya is a traditional Rajasthani tie-dye textile known for its wave-like patterns, inspired by the movement of desert winds.Also read: 80th Independence Day: 'Vande Mataram' played for first time as PM Modi addresses nation Modi wore a multicoloured Rajasthani-style bandhani turban in 2023, featuring shades of yellow, green and red. The Prime Minister paired it with an off-white kurta-churidar, a black V-neck jacket and a geometric-patterned pocket square.In 2022, Modi aligned his Independence Day attire with the Har Ghar Tiranga campaign, wearing a white turban decorated with saffron and green stripes. He paired it with a white kurta-churidar and a baby-blue Nehru jacket.The headgear mirrored the colours of the national flag while retaining the traditional format associated with his Independence Day appearances.During the Covid-19 pandemic in 2021, Modi wore a saffron turban featuring bold red patterns and a long pink trail. He paired it with a white kurta, fitted churidar, deep blue jacket and a white scarf edged with a saffron border.The long trailing end remained a prominent feature of the headgear, continuing the distinctive visual style of his earlier Independence Day turbans.At the height of the Covid-19 pandemic, Modi chose a saffron-and-cream turban with an extended tail. He wore it with a white kurta and churidar, along with an orange-and-white stole that also served as a protective face covering.The ensemble combined his recurring use of traditional headgear with a practical response to the public-health circumstances of the time.In 2019, Modi wore a multicoloured safa featuring Rajasthan’s traditional leheriya wave pattern. The design created a ripple effect across the headgear and continued his use of regional textile traditions for the Independence Day occasion.In 2018, Modi returned to saffron, wearing a bright turban decorated with red patterns and a long trail that extended almost to his ankles.He paired the headgear with a white stole featuring a broad geometric-patterned border.Modi chose a vibrant yellow turban in 2017, featuring intricate traditional and geometric patterns woven across the fabric.The headgear combined bright red and yellow with a subtle golden criss-cross design.Also read: From bandhani to leheriya: PM Modi’s Independence Day turbans over the years In 2016, Modi embraced the classic tie-and-dye technique with a vibrant bandhej turban in bright pink and yellow. The headgear featured distinctive patterns and a long trailing end.The festive design reflected the Prime Minister’s preference for colourful traditional headgear during the Independence Day celebrations.In 2015, Modi wore a sunny yellow turban covered in a multicoloured criss-cross pattern combining red and deep green. The headgear featured a long trail extending towards his ankles, giving the traditional Rajasthani-style turban a prominent silhouette.It marked another early example of Modi using Independence Day attire to foreground Indian textile traditions.For his maiden Independence Day address as Prime Minister in 2014, Modi wore a bright red Jodhpuri bandhej turban with contrasting green accents.The Rajasthani-style headgear featured vivid orange, yellow and green tones and traditional patterns. That first Red Fort appearance established the colourful turban as a recurring element of Modi’s Independence Day wardrobe, a tradition that has continued through successive addresses.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi arrived at the Red Fort on Saturday wearing a striking red tie- and-dye turban. The turban featured intricate red, green and white patterns, reflecting styles associated with Rajasthani and Gujarati traditions. Since his first address as Prime Minister in 2014, he has chosen safas and turbans in a wide range of colours and patterns.

Article Title: “Some day” is today
Article Text:
Thirukkural with the Times explores real-world lessons from the classic Tamil text ‘Thirukkural’. Written by Tamil poet and philosopher Thiruvalluvar, the Kural consists of 1,330 short couplets of seven words each. This text is divided into three books with teachings on virtue, wealth, and love and is considered one of the great works ever on ethics and morality. The Kural has influenced scholars and leaders across social, political, and philosophical spheres.

Motivational speaker, author and diversity champion Bharathi Bhaskar explores the masterpiece.

Last week, our college friend group of eleven girls lost one of our own. Through our four years in college, we had become inseparable. Three decades later, we were still together.And then, Devi was no more.For two years, she fought cancer bravely. She was the first to wish us on birthdays and anniversaries. We would wake to find her messages, often at 5.30 in the morning. Her love was like dawn. It brightened the lives of all around her. Her smile seemed to rise from the altar of her heart.We wept. Yet, strangely, there is also a quiet peace in knowing that she may now be in a place without pain. Where that place is, none of us know. But perhaps the more important realisation is that all of us are travelling towards it, each at our own pace.Losing someone we love shakes up our lives. Guilt arrives uninvited, whispering about words left unsaid and things left undone. Then life, with its extraordinary insistence, pulls us back. There are mails to send, vessels to wash, clothes to fold, work to finish. We think we are moving on, until suddenly, it returns, and we are thrown back into the tide of longing.Perhaps that is because love does not leave as easily as a person does.And perhaps the people we have loved have not entirely left us. Are they watching us? Are they closer than before? Sometimes I imagine them as passengers who have quietly got down from the train before us, without the chance to say goodbye. We continue our journey, carrying their memories with us.Younger colleagues approach the world differently. At home, children no longer listen to us. But with school and college friends, time seems to freeze.That is our safe haven. When one of us leaves that circle, however, we suddenly become conscious of the passing years.Valluvar captured this truth with remarkable simplicity in Kural 334:“Naalena Ondrupol Kaatti, UyirerumVaaladhu Unarvaar Perin.”“Every day appears to be merely a day, but to those who understand, it is a sword quietly cutting away a portion of life.”In the Mahabharata, Yudhishthira is asked by the Yaksha, “What is the strangest thing in the world?”He replies, “Countless beings leave the world every day, yet those who remain believe they will remain forever.” What greater wonder could there be?But perhaps this need not frighten us. It can awaken us, instead.Every day is a flower that blooms for exactly one day. The July rain, the December chill, the fragrance of neem in summer; all carry a beauty that will never return in precisely the same form.The lesson is not to fear the passing of days, but to live them fully. To laugh a little. To say what we keep postponing. To savour the morning light and coffee.Kahlil Gibran asks, “You want to know the secret of death. But how shall you find it unless you seek it in the heart of life?”That is where the answer lies.Not in knowing how the journey ends, but in making every day of the journey luminous.Devi did that for many of us. I will remember her; not as someone who has left, but as someone who taught us quietly how much radiance one life can leave behind.
Article Summary: Bharathi Bhaskar explores real-world lessons from the classic Tamil text ‘Thirukkural’ Written by Tamil poet and philosopher Thiruvalluvar, the Kural consists of 1,330 short couplets of seven words each.

Q: You point out that there are these rather horrific incidents which are almost genocidal.

Sunil Amrith is the Renu and Anand Dhawan Professor of History at Yale University with a secondary appointment as professor at the Yale School of the Environment. He serves as Director of the Macmillan Centre for International and Area Studies and Yale's Vice Provost for International Affairs.He has received the 2016 Infosys Prize in Humanities, a 2017 MacArthur Fellowship, and the 2025 Toynbee Prize in Global History, among others. He has authored five books that put Asia at the heart of global history. In this conversation, he discusses his book, 'The Burning Earth'.It was a coming together of my academic life and the rest of my life. For close to 20 years, I had been researching some of the themes that do make it into 'The Burning Earth'. I've particularly been interested in the relationship between migration, the movement of people and environmental change. So I wrote a book more than 10 years ago called 'Crossing the Bay of Bengal', which I think was my first foray into environmental history, in which I was really thinking about the enormous movement of people, particularly from Tamil Nadu, to southeast Asia in the 19th and 20th century, many of them to work on rubber plantations, but also to work in port cities, places like Singapore and Penang and Rangoon, and understanding that that was actually a moment of fundamental transformation in the environment... At the same time, as a teacher, but also as a parent, as a citizen, the climate crisis became quite unavoidable in my own consciousness. And so for me, that prompted me to scale things up beyond my areas of specialisation towards perhaps the biggest question, which is how did we get to this point of planetary crisis? And that's really what's at the heart of 'The Burning Earth'.If the question is what is it about my own perspective that may make this book a little bit different from some of the other books out there on this big theme of the environment, it is the fact that my own training is not in European and North American history. And I think most of what is called global history continues to take as its starting point and as its default, a kind of familiar North Atlantic history. And so by starting the book in China and ending it in Indonesia, I was really trying to write it anchored in Asia. .. Asia has always been home to the majority of humanity. It still is today. And so it seemed to me completely fitting to really think about the history of this planet with a firm anchor in the part of the world, the part of the planet which has been the most inhabited by most people throughout the longest period of time.That's the biggest challenge of a book like this. There's no possibility that I can have the primary expertise in all of these areas that I write about in the book. And so in some ways that was a leap that I took. Academia is a collective enterprise. And this is very much a book that builds on my own work in some areas. And in other areas, it's really sort of bringing together my reading in multiple fields of scholarship and different disciplines as well. So I'm a historian, but some of the most exciting new scholarship which I draw on and interpret is actually coming from the physical sciences.There's some phenomenally interesting work in paleoclimatology, for example, which is trying to reconstruct past climates using ice cores, using lake bed sediment, using tree rings. And of course, these disciplines traditionally and even still within the walls of the university barely meet. But what's been very interesting about recent work on climate and environment in particular, is you have this forcing together of completely different ideas of what the archive is.I don't use the word that many times, but when I do, I think it's doing a lot of work for me. 'The Burning Earth' is not an activist book, which is to say that it is just that bit muddier and less clear about the villains of the piece than activist writing necessarily has to be. And yet there is such a strong core in my own thinking of awareness of just how stark environmental inequalities are and just how much the scale of planetary destruction that has been achieved over the last two centuries has been disproportionately, not exclusively, but disproportionately driven by the elite pursuit of luxuries and of accumulation. .. There is a story of human need in this book and there's also a story of human greed... I think we need to think about desire, we need to think about states, we need to think about liberation, we need to think about the genuinely liberatory promises that led to some of this environmental destruction which can't be reduced to a question of greed or even of capitalism...There's no question that the social and economic system that has been a driving force in the climate crisis is the capitalist system. But the socialist system in some sense was even more environmentally profligate and wasteful. It was just less successful. And so in terms of its longevity, in terms of the scale on which it was operating, it kind of doesn't compare with what a particular capitalist mode of production does to our ability to treat all of nature as commodity and to lead to this kind of constantly expanding frontier of production.But my question is really a different one, which is, where were the alternatives? Who was thinking differently?I think that's one of the key narratives in the book to show that the moments of the most intensive and accelerated environmental destruction over the last several hundred years have almost always gone together with moments of intense violence. And violence is at the core of 'The Burning Earth'. Not just violence against the earth or against nature, but against other people... Wars that are going on all around us in the world today are part of a very long pattern where armed violence and militarism and military destruction have been inextricably bound with massive environmental destruction.
Article Summary: Sunil Amrith is the Renu and Anand Dhawan Professor of History at Yale University. He has authored five books that put Asia at the heart of global history. In this conversation, he discusses his book, 'The Burning Earth'

Article Title: SC quashes all FIRs against Samay Raina, Ranveer Allahabadia in ‘India’s Got Latent’ case
Article Text:
SC quashes all FIRs against Samay Raina, Ranveer Allahbadia

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday closed criminal proceedings against comedian Samay Raina and four other social media personalities over remarks concerning people with disabilities, while recognising their subsequent efforts to promote awareness and dignity for the community.Along with Raina, the court quashed the FIRs and related proceedings against comedians Vipul Goyal, Balraj Paramjeet Singh Ghai, Sonali Thakkar and Nishant Jagdish Tanwar.The proceedings stemmed from jokes made by the five, which were flagged by the M/s SMA Cure Foundation, an organisation working with people affected by Spinal Muscular Atrophy and other rare diseases.The case took a different turn after the Supreme Court asked the influencers to take constructive steps towards supporting people with disabilities. The court noted that they had since organised a chess tournament for specially-abled people in March and helped raise awareness about organisations working with people with disabilities.The bench, comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, said their efforts appeared to be producing positive results."Once there are genuine efforts, positive results are bound to be there," the bench said as per news agency PTI."They are very bright youngsters. If they have started working in the positive direction, they will bring positive results," it added.Senior advocate Aparajita Singh, appearing for the SMA Cure Foundation, told the court that the influencers had made "genuine efforts" and had attempted to engage with the foundation following the court's earlier intervention."This matter was going nowhere till this court took a very strong stand last time," Singh said.The court subsequently quashed the FIRs and other criminal proceedings against the five and said their case was now closed.However, the Supreme Court said it would separately examine the larger question of how the dignity of people with disabilities can be better protected and whether comprehensive directions are required.The court's observations came a day after the CJI and other judges met a delegation of people with disabilities from different fields."It was quite a learning and an eye-opener for us also," the CJI said, adding, "We have requested them to send their suggestions also.""It was quite a satisfying experience what we saw yesterday and what we interacted," he said.The delegation included 20 people, among them Paralympians and athletes such as Nidhi Mishra, Ankur Dhama and Major D P Singh, as well as Chhonzin Angmo.During Friday's hearing, the bench also noted that the influencers had engaged in meaningful discussions with the SMA Cure Foundation and were willing to invite people living with SMA to their shows.More programmes are also planned to raise funds for people affected by the condition.The influencers had earlier volunteered before the Supreme Court in November to organise at least two events every month, either online or in person, to raise money for a proposed corpus that could provide financial assistance to people living with SMA.The court's decision therefore brings the criminal proceedings against the five to an end, while leaving the broader question of protecting the dignity of people with disabilities open for further consideration.
Article Summary: SC quashes all FIRs against Samay Raina, Ranveer Allahbadia, Vipul Goyal, Balraj Paramjeet Singh Ghai, Sonali Thakkar and Nishant Jagdish Tanwar. The court noted that they had since organised a chess tournament for specially-abled people in March and helped raise awareness about organisations working with people with disabilities.

Article Title: Justice Yashwant Varma cash-at-home row: Can Parliament still remove judge from office?
Article Text:
. Justice Varma had on April 10 resigned as a judge of Allahabad High Court and had withdrawn from the inquiry proceedings

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: There is little chance of the Lok Sabha continuing with Justice Varma’s removal motion despite the inquiry committee finding the charges relating to discovery of unaccounted currency notes in his official residential premises proved.As per Article 217(1) of the Constitution, a judge ceases to hold office if he/she resigns by sending a resignation letter written “under his hand addressed to the President”. Justice Varma had on April 10 resigned as a judge of Allahabad High Court and had withdrawn from the inquiry proceedings, finding the writing on the wall.How does a resignation of a constitutional court judge take effect? This question was answered by a five-judge bench of the SC in the Gopal Chandra Misra case on Feb 15, 1978. It was unanimous that once the judge sends his resignation to the President, he/she is deemed to have ceased to be a judge.In that case, the judge had set a prospective date for his resignation taking effect and before the arrival of the appointed date, he had withdrawn his resignation. SC had by four to one majority ruled that since the resignation was prospective, the judge had every right to withdraw it prior to the appointed date.
Article Summary: Justice Varma had on April 10 resigned as a judge of Allahabad High Court and had withdrawn from the inquiry proceedings. As per Article 217(1) of the Constitution, a judge ceases to hold office if he/she resigns by sending a resignation letter written “under his hand addressed to the President’

Article Title: Ready for long debate, can answer any question but opposition doesn’t want it: Amit Shah
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Home minister Amit Shah on Wednesday flung a challenge at the opposition for a comprehensive debate over police action during the anti-NEET protests in Delhi on July 20, saying he was ready for a 24-hour-long debate in Parliament at an hour’s notice over their charge of police excesses against protesting students. He said govt had nothing to hide over an issue his rivals have used to attack him.“If they give their consent for discussion to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla at 2 pm, a debate can begin at 3 pm and go on till 3 pm the next day. I am ready to answer any question. But they (opposition) do not want debate to take place in Parliament. Let the people decide who is running away,” he told the media a day before the end of the monsoon session, which has been marred by the opposition’s disruptions over a host of issues. Soon after, parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said govt could even push for the session’s extension if the opposition wants.Shah said while the opposition had initially demanded his statement, govt had gone beyond it by agreeing to an extensive debate followed by his reply so that people could decide who was right and who was wrong.Amit Shah’s aggressive counter was seconded by a host of senior BJP functionaries, with party president Nitin Nabin saying the conduct of Rahul and the entire opposition was reflective of their “anarchic and anti-democracy” mindset.“The entire session is about to be over but they did not agree to a serious discussion over any issue,” he said, accusing them of running away after govt’s offer of a debate.With INDIA bloc MPs frequently accusing him of “running away” from Parliament, Shah hit back and said he was regularly in his chamber in the House. When the opposition was not letting the House function, what was the point of him going there, he asked.Expressing anguish at his opponents’ jibes like “lapata” (missing) and “bhagora” (fugitive) for him, Shah said these terms were being used only recently in parliamentary discourse.The minister later wrote to the Speaker, urging him to reach out to the opposition so that a discussion could begin. “You can allot as much time you think appropriate with mutual agreement. I want to participate in the discussion and I’m ready to answer every question of the opposition,” he said, adding that a solution to any issue in democracy emerged from dialogue and discussion.Congress had normalised disruption in Parliament, he said, adding a party which governed India for decades had fallen to such a low that it did not want discussion in the House.
Article Summary: Amit Shah said govt had nothing to hide over an issue his rivals have used to attack him. He said if they give their consent for discussion to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla at 2 pm, a debate can begin at 3 pm and go on till 3 pm the next day.

Article Title: The wholesome story of Fernando Mendoza: How the Raiders’ No. 1 pick went from Yale reject to Heisman winner
Article Text:
Fernando Mendoza to Raiders talk (Getty Images)

Fernando Mendoza's Full Story: From Under-Recruited Miami QB to Heisman Winner and No. 1 Overall Pick

The brother who brought him home

The payoff, and what's actually next

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Fernando Mendoza's first pro highlight reel dropped this week, and the internet is already comparing him to Tom Brady. Which is funny, because five years ago, college football didn't want him at all. Before the Heisman, before the Big Ten title, before becoming the Raiders' No. 1 overall pick, Mendoza was a kid so overlooked that his backup plan was Yale. Actual Yale. Not because he wasn't good but because nobody with a football budget was paying attention. What happened between then and now is less a highlight reel and more a slow, deliberate refusal to be underestimated, and it says a lot about who he is that the biggest headline of his rookie preseason debut isn't even about him, it's about his little brother.Mendoza was born in Boston, of all places, while his dad was finishing a medical residency, but the family moved home to Miami almost immediately, and that's where the story actually starts.He grew up Cuban-American with deep roots, his grandparents immigrated from Havana and Santiago, and he's called that heritage "a huge point of pride," even organizing a trip back to Cuba with his grandfather to reconnect with family and give back to the community.That kind of rootedness shows up later in how loyal he is to the people who back him.But as a recruit, he was basically invisible. He went to Christopher Columbus High School in Miami, put up real numbers, and still walked away with a grand total of one Power Five offer from Cal, and even that one only came late, after another quarterback backed out. His actual plan B was Yale. Let that sink in. The guy who'd eventually win the Heisman was one decommitment away from playing Ivy League football instead of major college ball.He took the Cal offer, redshirted, then spent two seasons starting and quietly became one of the most efficient passers in the conference with a 66.4% completion percentage, a program record. And still, somehow, still underrated. He was sacked more than any quarterback in the country one season and barely got a mention in national conversations.So he left. Not out of frustration, but calculation. He said flat out that he needed a system that could turn him into "a pro-ready quarterback," and Cal, as much as he loved it, wasn't going to get him there.Here's the part that makes this whole story hit different: the reason he landed at Indiana wasn't a coaching pitch or a facilities tour. It was his little brother.Alberto Mendoza, Fernando's younger brother, had already committed to Indiana as a backup quarterback, following head coach Curt Cignetti there after originally signing with him at James Madison.When Fernando entered the transfer portal, it was Alberto who talked him into Bloomington, telling him he knew "the good, the bad, the excellent" about the program. Cignetti later admitted the Alberto connection made recruiting Fernando "a pretty easy decision" the family already trusted him.So the two brothers ended up sharing a quarterback room, which is a genuinely rare college football plotline on its own. But what they did off the field is the part that actually gets us.Their family has a personal connection to multiple sclerosis, and instead of just talking about it, they turned it into an ongoing fundraiser. First, the "Mendoza Burrito" at a local spot near Cal; then, after the move, the "Mendoza Bros. Burger" and a "Mendoza Bros.Cubano" bagel sandwich in Bloomington. Small-town food gimmicks, sure, but they raised more than $66,000 for the National MS Society doing it. Before accepting his Heisman, Fernando used his platform again, partnering with Adidas to give four MS-affected families $10,000 each in shopping sprees.That's the thing about Mendoza that doesn't show up in scouting reports: the guy who was invisible to recruiters spent his rise making sure other people didn't stay invisible either.The Yale-adjacent underdog led Indiana to its first-ever 13-0 season and its first outright Big Ten title since 1945. He won the Heisman. He went No. 1 overall to the Raiders. And in his first professional preseason snaps this week, he looked exactly like the guy Vegas paid a premium for with sharp reads, a touchdown, no picks, and one absolute dart through three defenders that's already living on NFL Twitter.But somehow the moment that actually went viral from his debut wasn't the football. It was his little brother Max, a different, younger Mendoza sibling, getting invited into the commentary booth and having a moment with Tom Brady on air. Which, honestly, feels right. This is a family that's been quietly building each other up for years while the football world caught up. The NFL just finally noticed.
Article Summary: Fernando Mendoza won the Heisman and was picked No. 1 overall by the Raiders. He was overlooked as a high school quarterback, and his backup plan was Yale. The reason he landed at Indiana wasn't a coaching pitch or a facilities tour. It was his younger brother, Alberto.

Terrel Williams has kept a low profile since the 2015 fight that changed Prichard Colon’s life. Williams beat Colon by disqualification in the ninth round in Fairfax, Virginia, but Colon suffered a serious brain injury soon after and spent 221 days in a coma. Colon died on August 13, 2026, at 33, more than a decade after the fight. His death has brought fresh attention to the boxer who shared the ring with him that night. So, where is Terrel Williams now, and what happened to his boxing career? Those questions remain difficult to answer.Williams was unbeaten when he entered the ring against Colon on October 17, 2015. He won the fight after Colon’s corner removed his gloves at the end of the ninth round, believing the scheduled 10-round bout was over. The Premier Boxing Champions record confirms Williams won by disqualification after knocking Colon down twice in the ninth.The Washington Post reported that Colon had complained about punches to the back of his head during the bout. Williams was deducted a point in the seventh round for a rabbit punch. After the fight, Colon became dizzy and vomited in his dressing room before collapsing. He was taken to Inova Fairfax Hospital and needed emergency surgery for bleeding on the brain.Williams did not return to the ring for two years. ESPN reported in 2017 that his comeback was being planned after he had stayed away from boxing since the Colon fight. He returned in November that year and won by knockout against Rosemberg Gomez.Williams spoke about the emotional effect of the fight and made clear that he never wanted Colon to suffer such an injury.“I pray for Prichard every single day. I don’t wish nothing but peace and health for that man. It’s been hard on me, too. I didn’t want that to happen to him. I was just trying to win a fight. My life changed that night, and it will never be the same,” the boxer said.The Los Angeles Times also reported shortly after the fight that Williams was deeply affected by Colon’s condition. He said he felt compassion for Colon and his family and was focused on hoping the young boxer would recover.Williams later returned to boxing, but the comeback was short. His record shows four fights after the 2015 bout. He won three of them, including the 2017 comeback, before losing to Thomas Dulorme by unanimous decision on September 21, 2019.Williams is retired from professional boxing. The World Boxing Association lists his final record as 18-1 with 13 knockouts, while his last recorded fight came against Dulorme in 2019.There is little reliable public information about Williams’ life since retirement. He has largely stayed away from interviews and the boxing spotlight, and recent reporting has described him as difficult to reach. There is no clear public record showing that he has returned to boxing or taken on a major public role in the sport.That makes his present whereabouts difficult to confirm. The Colon fight remained the defining event of Williams’ career. More than 10 years later, the fight is again being discussed after Colon’s death at 33. The circumstances of Colon’s death have not been publicly detailed by his family or medical team, according to current reports.

Article Title: Ronaldo’s secret wedding rocked by new twist after leaked marriage certificate reveals 4 surprise witnesses
Article Text:
Leaked Ronaldo wedding certificate reveals four surprise witnesses in new twist to secret ceremony

Four witnesses were present at the ceremony

Ronaldo’s mother and sisters were absent

The five children were still at the centre of the wedding

Their marriage arrangements were also kept private

It was a very different wedding from the one fans expected

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Ronaldo returns as Al-Nassr season begins

Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodríguez kept their wedding deliberately small, but a newly surfaced marriage certificate has revealed that the ceremony was attended by more people than initially reported. The document shows that, alongside the couple’s five children, four witnesses were present when Ronaldo and Rodríguez formally married in a private civil ceremony in Cascais on August 11.The identities of those witnesses also provide a clearer picture of who was inside the intimate ceremony, and notably, Ronaldo’s mother Dolores Aveiro and his sisters Elma and Katia were not among them.The marriage certificate obtained by Portuguese newspaper Jornal de Notícias and reported on by Spanish media states that the ceremony took place at 1.30pm on Tuesday, August 11.The document names four witnesses: Miguel Paixão, Ivana Rodríguez, José Rodríguez Sangil and Mónica González Martínez.Paixão is a longstanding friend of Ronaldo dating back to the footballer’s youth at Sporting, while Ivana is Georgina’s sister. Rodríguez Sangil is described by the Portuguese press as a Spanish jeweller, with González Martínez identified as his wife.That means the ceremony was not attended solely by Ronaldo, Rodríguez and their five children, as earlier reports had suggested.There were four additional witnesses who were required to be present for the civil marriage.The ceremony itself was officiated by Maria Manuel Ferreira de Campos Folhadela de Oliveira, a registrar who travelled from Porto to Cascais to conduct the marriage.According to the certificate, the ceremony took place at the couple’s home in Cascais. A report from The Sun identified the property as Ronaldo’s approximately £30 million mansion in the Quinta da Marinha area, around 35 kilometres from Lisbon.The newly revealed guest details are particularly notable because none of Ronaldo’s immediate female family members were listed among the witnesses.His mother, Dolores Aveiro, was not present, nor were his sisters Elma Aveiro and Katia Aveiro.Ronaldo’s brother Hugo was also not among those listed.The absence of his mother is notable given her public support for the marriage. After Ronaldo announced the wedding on Instagram with a photograph of the couple’s wedding rings and the caption “C❤️G”, Dolores responded with a heart, publicly signalling her blessing for the union.There has also been speculation over the years about the relationship between Dolores and Rodríguez, although the family has previously pushed back against suggestions of a serious rift.The presence of the children remains consistent with the information previously provided by Ronaldo’s representative.When the marriage was first confirmed, the representative said Ronaldo and Rodríguez had married in a “private and intimate” civil ceremony in Cascais, adding that it was attended by their five children.Those children are Cristiano Jr, twins Eva and Mateo, Alana Martina and Bella.The new certificate does not contradict that account; rather, it adds four witnesses to the picture and identifies the people who were there in an official capacity for the civil ceremony.The result was still a remarkably small wedding for one of the world's most recognisable footballers.The certificate reveals another significant detail about how Ronaldo and Rodríguez organised their marriage.The couple chose a separation of property regime, meaning that, as a general rule, each spouse retains ownership of assets they already possessed before the marriage as well as property acquired afterwards.That arrangement is not the default marital regime in Portugal. The document shows that Ronaldo and Rodríguez therefore signed a prenuptial agreement on August 10, one day before the wedding, at a notary's office in Lisbon.The certificate also states that neither adopted the other's surname following the marriage. They continue to use their existing names and list Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, as their usual place of residence.The secrecy surrounding the ceremony became even more striking because of what happened only days earlier. Hundreds of supporters, journalists and tourists had gathered outside Funchal Cathedral in Madeira after reports claimed Ronaldo and Rodríguez would marry there. The footballer was born in Madeira, making the location an obvious focal point for fans hoping to see the couple.They were waiting for the wrong wedding.The ceremony at the cathedral belonged to another couple, Fabio Ramos and Fatima Nicole Cunha Teixeira, and Ronaldo himself later appeared to find the confusion amusing after footage circulated showing the crowds waiting outside for him and Rodríguez.The actual ceremony took place several days later, away from the crowds, at the couple’s home in Cascais.Ronaldo and Rodríguez had been together since 2016 and announced their engagement in August 2025.Ronaldo and Rodríguez were spotted at Lisbon’s Humberto Delgado Airport on Thursday with their children, reportedly heading back to Saudi Arabia. The 41-year-old is now set to return to Al-Nassr as the club begins its 2026–27 season on August 15, with their Saudi Pro League opener against Al-Fateh at Al-Awwal Park in Riyadh at 11:30pm IST.And footage has since emerged of Ronaldo being congratulated by his teammates following his wedding, with the Portuguese star proudly wearing his new wedding ring as he returns to football duties.
Article Summary: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodríguez kept their wedding deliberately small. A newly surfaced marriage certificate has revealed that the ceremony was attended by more people than initially reported. Ronaldo’s mother, Dolores Aveiro, was not present, nor were his sisters Elma and Katia Aveiro. There were four additional witnesses who were required to be present.

Article Title: What happened to Chinedu Ozor? Did the Nigerian soccer player wake up at mortuary after being pronounced dead?
Article Text:
Chinedu Ozor. Image via: Katsina United/Instagram

What really happened to Chinedu Ozor

Did Chinedu Ozor wake up after being pronounced dead?

Katsina United's statement addresses the confusion

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A career cut short just as it was beginning again

Chinedu Ozor, the 27-year-old Nigerian defender who collapsed during a preseason friendly on Tuesday, did not wake up after being pronounced dead, according to his club, Katsina United. The team confirmed his death and directly refuted widespread reports claiming he showed signs of life at the mortuary.Ozor went down nine minutes into a match against Niger Tornadoes at Muhammadu Dikko Stadium in Katsina. He was rushed to K-Dara Specialist Hospital, where he was pronounced dead, triggering a wave of tributes across Nigerian football before a second wave of confusion followed.The collapse happened in the opening minutes of what was meant to be a routine preseason tune-up. Chinedu Ozor had just completed a move to Katsina United from Kano Pillars ahead of the 2026/27 Nigerian Premier Football League season, and Tuesday's match against Niger Tornadoes was part of his integration into the squad.He went down suddenly, and medical staff on site were unable to revive him. He was pronounced dead at the hospital shortly after.Hours after the initial announcement, several Nigerian and international outlets, including the Lagos-based Guardian, reported that a morgue attendant had noticed Ozor's hand moving and raised the alarm, prompting his return to the hospital and placement on oxygen.Some of Ozor's former clubs, including Heartland, even issued statements referencing the apparent development. Those reports spread quickly across football circles in Nigeria and beyond, but they were not accurate. Katsina United later clarified that no revival occurred and that Ozor's death was final.Katsina United acknowledged the emotional weight of the moment directly. "There are moments when words simply fail us," the club wrote in a follow-up statement on X, before addressing the false reports head-on. The club added that it understood why people wanted the story to be true, but confirmed it was not, and asked for compassion for the family rather than continued speculation. “We have seen reports claiming that Chinedu later regained consciousness or ‘came back to life. ’ We understand that people desperately wanted this to be true. We all did. But sadly, those reports are not true,” the team wrote on X.The team further urged privacy for the family. “At this moment, what his family needs is compassion, not speculation. What his teammates need is space to grieve. And what Chinedu deserves is to be remembered with dignity.”Katsina State Governor Malam Dikko Umaru Radda also issued a statement mourning Ozor's death. "It is particularly painful that a young footballer with a promising career" had his life cut short at this stage of his career, the governor said, extending condolences to Ozor's family, Katsina United, and the wider football community, including Kano Pillars.Ozor's move to Katsina United was meant to mark a fresh chapter, arriving from Kano Pillars with the new NPFL season on the horizon.Tuesday's friendly against Niger Tornadoes was supposed to be a low-stakes step in that transition. Instead, it became the final match of his career, and Nigerian football is now left processing both his death and the misinformation that briefly clouded it.
Article Summary: Chinedu Ozor, 27, collapsed during a preseason friendly on Tuesday. He was rushed to a hospital, where he was pronounced dead. Reports claimed he showed signs of life at the mortuary. His club, Katsina United, confirmed his death and refuted the reports.

Article Title: Jimmy Rimmer dies at 78: Tributes pour in for the Manchester United and Aston Villa star, exploring the European Cup winner career’s best highlights
Article Text:
Jimmy Rimmer (Image via Arsenal)

Jimmy Rimmer death : Aston Villa pays tribute to the veteran goalkeeper

Inside Jimmy Rimmer’s remarkable career with Manchester United and Aston Villa

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former Manchester United and Aston Villa goalkeeper Jimmy Rimmer has passed away at the age of 78. The veteran goalkeeper enjoyed a career spanning more than two decades. He won the European Cup with both clubs.Rimmer was part of United’s historic 1968 European Cup-winning squad. He later became a key player for Aston Villa. He started their European Cup campaign in 1982 and helped them reach the final against Bayern Munich.Aston Villa confirmed his death in a statement and described him as a European Cup winner. The club also expressed its sympathy to his family and friends. His cause of death has not been publicly revealed.“Aston Villa is deeply saddened to learn of the passing of European Cup winner Jimmy Rimmer, who has died at the age of 78. The thoughts of everyone at the club are with Jimmy’s family and friends at this incredibly difficult time”, the team’s statement read.Former United teammate Alex Stepney also paid tribute. He remembered Rimmer with affection and sent his condolences to the goalkeeper’s family. “Such sad news to hear Jimmy Rimmer has passed away, rest in peace and lots of love to Jimmy’s family x”, he wrote.Born in Southport, Lancashire, Rimmer joined Manchester United as a schoolboy in 1963. He turned professional two years later and eventually became part of Sir Matt Busby’s first-team squad.Rimmer spent much of his United career as the understudy to Alex Stepney. He was on the bench when United made history in 1968 by beating Benfica 4-1 after extra time at Wembley. The victory made United the first English club to lift the European Cup.After more than a decade connected with United, Rimmer moved to Arsenal in 1974. His time in north London also brought him international recognition. He earned his only England cap in a friendly against Italy.His career changed significantly when he joined Aston Villa in 1977. Manager Ron Saunders signed him for around £65,000. Rimmer quickly established himself as Villa’s first-choice goalkeeper.He made 287 appearances for Villa in all competitions between 1977 and 1983. He was also part of the side that won the First Division title in the 1980-81 season.Rimmer’s greatest Villa moment came during the 1981-82 European Cup campaign. He played in every match on the road to the final. However, he suffered a neck injury during the final against Bayern Munich in Rotterdam. The 1982 European Cup medal was therefore the second of Rimmer’s career. His first had come as part of Manchester United’s 1968 triumph.After leaving Villa in 1983, Rimmer returned to Swansea City. He later had short spells with Hamrun Spartans and Luton Town in 1986 before ending his playing career.Rimmer also spent time coaching in countries including China and Canada.Rimmer leaves behind a unique legacy. He was part of two European Cup-winning teams with two different English clubs. His contribution to Aston Villa’s greatest European triumph will remain an important part of the club’s history.
Article Summary: Former Manchester United and Aston Villa goalkeeper Jimmy Rimmer has passed away at the age of 78. The veteran goalkeeper enjoyed a career spanning more than two decades. Rimmer was part of United’s historic 1968 European Cup-winning squad. He later became a key player for Aston Villa and started their European Cup campaign in 1982.

Article Title: 800 kmph in 5.3 seconds: China train sets third record in six months
Article Text:
The 1,110-kg test vehicle, developed at Donghu Laboratory, achieved the milestone in its latest trial

How China’s experimental maglev works

Why reaching 800 kmph is so difficult

Could maglev technology launch rockets?

China has pushed maglev technology into a speed range far beyond conventional high-speed rail, with an experimental train car reaching 800 kmph in only 5.3 seconds on a 1-km test track in Hubei.The 1,110-kg test vehicle, developed at Donghu Laboratory, achieved the milestone in its latest trial, marking its third world record in six months.The experiment, however, is not aimed at putting passengers on trains travelling at 800 kmph.Instead, the technology could eventually have applications in rocketry, military aircraft, drones and industrial transport, where extremely rapid acceleration could be more useful.Unlike conventional trains, maglev vehicles use magnetic forces to reduce or eliminate physical contact between the train and the track. Electromagnetic systems can both levitate the vehicle and propel it forward.China's fastest commercial maglev service, the Fuxing system, has a top speed of about 217 mph (349 kmph. The experimental Donghu Laboratory vehicle is therefore operating at more than twice that speed.The latest test was carried out on a 1-km-long track in Hubei. According to CGTN, the system worked like a giant slingshot: magnetic forces propel the vehicle forward while eliminating the friction associated with conventional rail travel.The test vehicle has already broken its own short-distance acceleration record multiple times. Its first public run in June 2025 reached about 404 mph (650 kmph) in 7.1 seconds.Engineers subsequently raised the speed to about 433 mph (697 kmph) before reaching nearly 496 mph (798 kmph) in November.At such speeds, even tiny deviations in the track can become a major engineering challenge.The experimental system reportedly requires track alignment to remain within 0.5 millimetres.Control systems must simultaneously manage the vehicle's position, levitation and electromagnetic propulsion while maintaining stability during rapid acceleration.The vehicle weighs around 1,110 kg, meaning enormous amounts of energy and force are required to accelerate it to such speeds within seconds.The trials have also helped researchers test technologies involving high-power energy delivery, levitation control, positioning, electromagnetic propulsion and emergency braking.The biggest significance of the experiment may lie beyond railways.Passenger trains travelling at such speeds would require expensive infrastructure and enormous energy inputs, while acceleration levels involved in the tests would not be suitable for conventional commuter travel.Researchers are therefore exploring whether similar electromagnetic acceleration technology could eventually be adapted for rockets, drones and military aircraft.A ground-based launch system capable of giving a rocket or aircraft a substantial initial boost could potentially reduce the amount of fuel it needs to carry for take-off. Similar technology could also find applications in industrial transport and specialised elevators.For now, the technology remains experimental. China's commercial maglev systems already demonstrate that magnetic levitation can deliver very high-speed passenger transport, but the leap from those systems to an 800-kmph experimental vehicle represents a very different engineering challenge.
Article Summary: The 1,110-kg test vehicle, developed at Donghu Laboratory, achieved the milestone in its latest trial. It is China's third world record in six months. The technology could eventually have applications in rocketry, military aircraft, drones and industrial transport.

Why Bengals star Orlando Brown Jr.’s ex Holly is suing him for more than $25K?

Orlando Brown Jr. has a different version of what actually happened

Orlando Brown Jr.’s breakup has now turned into a legal fight. Holly Means, the Cincinnati Bengals offensive tackle’s ex-girlfriend, has sued him over property she says he has refused to return. She is seeking more than $25,000 in damages, along with the return of her property and punitive damages, according to court documents reported by TMZ on August 13, 2026.The lawsuit comes after their relationship ended in June 2025. Holly and Brown have two children together, and she says the problems began when she left their Ohio home and could not collect everything she owned. Brown denies wrongdoing and disputes her version of events.Orlando Brown Jr.’s ex, Holly says she lived with Brown and their two children at his Ohio home until their June 2025 breakup. According to her lawsuit, Brown forced her out without notice, leaving her unable to collect all of her personal belongings.She claims the property did not stay in one place. Some of her belongings, she says, ended up in Oklahoma and Kansas City. Holly alleges that Brown then blocked her efforts to retrieve them, including attempts to collect property from a storage unit.The dispute continued into Jan. 2026. Holly says she went to Brown’s Ohio home with police to collect her belongings. She claims Brown knew why she had arrived but refused to answer the door.Holly alleges Brown acted out of “anger and spite” following their breakup and her decision to move with their children back to Oregon. She also claims he acted with “ill will or a spirit of revenge.”She is asking for more than $25,000 in damages, the return of her property and punitive damages. TMZ reports that Holly filed the case as a civil theft lawsuit.Brown strongly disputes those claims. He says Holly came to his home unannounced after he had asked her not to come there. He also argues that she abandoned the property after their separation and has asked the court to dismiss the lawsuit with prejudice.The lawsuit follows a relationship that had been public for several years. Brown and Holly, who was previously known publicly as Holly Luyah, began sharing their relationship publicly around 2019. They later started a family and have two sons together.Their second child, Sonny, was born in December 2023. CBS Pittsburgh reported that Brown was in Pittsburgh preparing to play the Steelers when Holly went into labour early, and he watched the birth through FaceTime before playing that game. Their relationship ultimately ended in June 2025, according to Holly’s lawsuit.Orlando Brown’s response puts the focus on what happened after the breakup. He denies that he wrongfully kept Holly’s property and says she came to his home without an appointment after he had told her not to.His legal position also challenges Holly’s claim that he deliberately kept her belongings from her. Brown argues that she abandoned the property when she left following their split. He is asking the court to dismiss the case with prejudice.That means the court has two conflicting accounts of the same dispute. Holly says Brown prevented her from getting her property because of anger over the breakup. Brown says she left the items behind and later came to his home without his permission.Currently, Holly’s accusations remain allegations. There has been no court finding that Brown committed civil theft or acted with ill will, and Brown continues to deny wrongdoing. The lawsuit will determine what happens next.

Article Title: Prichard Colon dies at 33: Anger grows online as Terrel Williams’ alleged Instagram account is targeted
Article Text:
Prichard Colon dies at 33: Anger grows online as Terrel Williams’ alleged Instagram account is targeted

Terrel Williams faces online hate after Prichard Colon’s death

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

What did Terrel Williams say about Prichard Colon?

Prichard Colon’s death has brought the painful 2015 boxing fight back into sharp public focus, and Terrel Williams is again facing anger online. Colon died on August 13, 2026, at 33, almost 11 years after suffering a severe brain injury in his bout with Williams. After the news spread, users began leaving abusive comments on an Instagram account they believe belongs to Williams, although the account itself is not verified.Colon and Williams fought on October 17, 2015, in Fairfax, Virginia. The fight became controversial after Williams landed illegal punches behind Colon’s head. The Washington Post reported that Colon complained about the blows and was examined by ringside doctor Richard Ashby after a seventh-round incident. He continued fighting.The fight ended after nine rounds when Colon’s corner mistakenly began removing his gloves, thinking the bout was over. He was disqualified. Soon after reaching his dressing room, Colon became dizzy, vomited and collapsed. He needed emergency surgery for bleeding in his brain.Colon spent 221 days in a coma and later remained in a vegetative state, needing care for the rest of his life. His father, Richard Colon, announced his death on August 13.The cause of death has not been publicly disclosed, according to People.Williams was investigated by Virginia’s Department of Professional and Occupational Regulation. The investigation did not find one action serious enough to blame a single person.Williams was not named as a defendant in the $50 million lawsuit filed by Colon’s parents in 2017. The case targeted ringside doctor Richard Ashby and the fight promoters, according to ESPN and The Washington Post.The Washington Post reported in 2019 that Williams had shut down his social media accounts after facing backlash over the fight.In 2019, Williams told The Washington Post he wanted to speak with Colon’s parents, but believed they would not want contact with him.Following Colon’s death, users searched for him again and posted hateful comments under an Instagram account allegedly linked to him.There is no verified public Instagram account confirming that the profile belongs to Williams, so those comments do not prove he runs the page.Williams has spoken about Colon’s condition and the emotional effect of the fight, but has not formally apologized or accepted blame. In a 2018 interview with The Ring, he said he prayed for Colon every day and did not want what happened to him.“I pray for Prichard every day. That’s never going to change. I wish him nothing but peace and health,” Williams said, according to The Ring.Williams said he never intended to seriously hurt Colon and that the night changed his life. He returned to boxing after taking about two years away from the sport and later fought Thomas Dulorme in 2019, his final professional bout.Colon’s death has put the fight back in the spotlight. Still, the facts remain: the Virginia investigation did not assign blame to him, and the family’s civil lawsuit did not name him as a defendant.

Article Title: 'Clubs struggling to survive': Former India captain blasts AIFF's ASEAN Cup call to play Brazil friendly
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Indian football great Bhaichung Bhutia has questioned the All India Football Federation's decision to withdraw from the inaugural FIFA ASEAN Cup to play a friendly against Brazil, saying the reported Rs 50-70 crore cost of the match is difficult to justify while Indian clubs are facing financial problems.India are scheduled to play five-time world champions Brazil in Kolkata on October 3. The AIFF chose the friendly over the FIFA ASEAN Cup after the two commitments created a scheduling clash.Bhutia said he had no issue with Brazil visiting India for a free friendly but questioned spending such a large amount on the match at this stage."If Brazil were coming free of cost to play a free friendly match, I have no problem with that. But to pay Brazil Rs 50-70 crore to come and play a friendly in India at this moment, the timing is not right. The timing is completely wrong," Bhutia said, while talking to news agency PTI.He also criticised AIFF president Kalyan Chaubey, accusing the federation leadership of "completely misguiding" the government and people involved in Indian football."Why do you want to pay Rs 50-70 crore at this moment when ISL clubs are shutting down, club after club, and I-League clubs are struggling to pay their entry fees?" he asked.Bhutia's comments come at a time when Indian club football is dealing with financial and administrative issues. The previous commercial arrangement between the AIFF and Football Sports Development Limited (FSDL) over the Indian Super League (ISL) faced uncertainty as its Master Rights Agreement neared expiry. The 2025-26 ISL season was delayed before eventually beginning in a shortened format after intervention from the Sports Ministry.Tata Steel also exited Jamshedpur FC, with the club transferred to Churchill Brothers for a symbolic Rs 100 on Friday.India had initially accepted FIFA's invitation to take part in the new ASEAN Cup and were drawn in Division 1 Group A with Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore. The tournament is scheduled during the September 21-October 6 FIFA international window.However, India's October 3 friendly against Brazil at Kolkata's Salt Lake Stadium created a clash with the tournament."We have such a wonderful tournament, a FIFA-recognised event that is most probably a calendar event every two to four years, and to miss all that just to play one friendly and pay Rs 50-70 crore -- that is such bad timing," he said, as quoted by PTI."You have a federation struggling with money at the moment, and then the AIFF wants to pay an advance fee to Brazil from that amount. I think it is such a bad decision."Bhutia also believes the ASEAN Cup would have given India more competitive matches against teams from the region, including Thailand, Indonesia, Vietnam, Malaysia and Singapore."It is a FIFA-recognised tournament and has teams like Thailand, Indonesia, Vietnam, Malaysia and Singapore, who have beaten us in Asia and World Cup qualifiers," he said.He added that Brazil could still visit India in the future if the federation is prepared to spend on a high-profile friendly."Brazil can always come. Argentina, Spain, France can always come and play in India when you are paying that kind of money. You can get any team to come and play, but at the moment I think the timing is wrong."
Article Summary: Bhaichung Bhutia questions All India Football Federation's decision to withdraw from the inaugural FIFA ASEAN Cup to play a friendly against Brazil. India are scheduled to play five-time world champions Brazil in Kolkata on October 3. The AIFF chose the friendly over the FIFA A SEAN Cup after the two commitments created a scheduling clash.

Australia fast bowler Mitchell Starc and Bangladesh all-rounder Mehidy Hasan Miraz had an exchange during a tense end to the second day of the first Test in Darwin on Friday.The incident took place during Starc's 21st over, the 103rd over of Bangladesh's innings. Miraz hit the ball towards point and set off for a single, but while following the ball, appeared to run through the protected area in the middle of the pitch.Umpire Kumar Dharmasena immediately stepped in and warned Miraz about running on the centre strip.Miraz explained that he had not seen Starc because he was watching the ball. Starc was unhappy with the explanation and told the Bangladesh batter to stay away from the protected area.Batters, like bowlers, are expected to avoid the protected central area of the pitch. Bowlers must stay away from it during their follow-through, while batters are expected to avoid it when running between the wickets.Miraz initially looked towards Starc as he started running, but then turned his attention to the ball. When he looked forward again, he was almost face-to-face with Starc.Rather than going around the fast bowler, Miraz took the shorter route through the centre of the pitch, prompting Dharmasena to intervene before the run had been completed.Miraz then raised his arm towards Starc and explained that he could not see where he was going while watching the ball.“It’s my follow-through, now your follow-through. Get off the wicket,” Starc could be heard saying while pointing at the Bangaldesh right-hander.“I can’t see, I can’t see. I didn’t see,” Miraz explained to Dharmasena.As Starc walked back to his mark, he could again be heard saying: “You’re not in Bangladesh now, hey?”Former Australia captain and Channel 7 commentator Ricky Ponting felt Miraz had not deliberately run through the protected area.“Yeah, I’m not sure that was on purpose,” Ponting said.“By the time he looked up, Starc was in his way and he just opted to go the centre of the wicket side of the fast bowler.”Bangladesh ended Day 2 in control, reaching 6-351 and taking a 153-run first-innings lead with four wickets still in hand.Miraz was unbeaten on 32, while Hasan Mahmud was 13 not out from 76 balls. Hasan had taken six wickets on the opening day.Tanzid Hasan, playing only his second Test, scored 101 to put Bangladesh in a position to push for what could become their biggest win in Test cricket.

Article Title: Did Sam Darnold really leapfrog Lamar Jackson and Joe Burrow in the NFL Top 100?
Article Text:
Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold climbed from No. 72 to No. 21 in the player-voted NFL Top 100 after winning Super Bowl LX. (Image via Getty)

Why did NFL players rank Sam Darnold above Lamar Jackson and Joe Burrow?

Has Sam Darnold finally killed the biggest criticism of his NFL career?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Sam Darnold spent years trying to outrun one label after another. NFL players have now placed him ahead of Lamar Jackson, Joe Burrow, Justin Herbert and Dak Prescott.The NFL revealed Darnold at No. 21 on its 2026 NFL Top 100 list, a 51-place jump from his No. 72 debut last year. The annual ranking is voted on by NFL players, making the company Darnold now keeps one of the more striking results of this year's list.The names below Darnold make No. 21 difficult to ignore.Jackson, a two-time NFL MVP, landed at No. 69. Burrow came in at No. 44, Herbert at No. 39 and Prescott at No. 31. Darnold entered the top 25 after finishing his first season with the Seattle Seahawks as a Super Bowl champion.His regular-season numbers provided a strong case. Darnold completed 67.7% of his passes for 4,048 yards and 25 touchdowns as Seattle went 14-3 and secured the NFC's No. 1 seed. He made the Pro Bowl for the second consecutive season.There was still one familiar problem. Darnold threw 14 interceptions and remained vulnerable when pressure forced him into mistakes. NFL Pro data cited by the league showed that he committed a turnover on 7.2% of his pressured dropbacks, the highest rate in the NFL.That makes his postseason especially important to understanding the ranking.Darnold threw for 672 yards and five touchdowns across three playoff victories without committing a turnover. His postseason passer rating was 102.5, and Seattle became the first Super Bowl champion to finish an entire postseason without turning the ball over.His biggest test came before the Super Bowl. Darnold threw for 346 yards and three touchdowns in Seattle's 31-27 NFC Championship Game win over the Los Angeles Rams, answering one of the questions that had followed him from Minnesota.Seattle coach Mike Macdonald summed up the reaction afterward.“You can't talk about the game without talking about our quarterback,” Macdonald said. “He just shut a lot of people up tonight. Really happy for him.”That performance gave Darnold something his 2024 breakout with the Minnesota Vikings could not: a postseason result that matched the regular-season production.Darnold's rise did not begin in Seattle. He threw for 4,319 yards and 35 touchdowns while winning 14 games with Minnesota in 2024, earning his first Pro Bowl selection. His final two games changed the conversation.Minnesota lost to the Detroit Lions in Week 18 with the NFC North title and No. 1 seed at stake. The Vikings then lost their wild-card game against the Rams, with Darnold taking nine sacks. Seattle still signed him to a three-year, $100.5 million contract after trading Geno Smith to the Las Vegas Raiders.One year later, the gamble looks very different.Darnold led another team to 14 wins, won the NFC West, reached another Pro Bowl and then delivered three turnover-free postseason victories. The last of those ended with Seattle beating the New England Patriots in Super Bowl LX.Macdonald addressed the years of discussion around his quarterback after the title.“Sam doesn't care about the obstacles,” Macdonald said. “Everyone's made a narrative of this guy, they have tried to put a story and a label on who he is as a person and who he is as a quarterback.”Darnold appears less interested in closing the argument himself.“I think I can always get better,” Darnold said early in training camp.He specifically pointed to his footwork, progression speed and throws he wanted back from the Super Bowl. That matters heading into 2026 because No. 21 does not erase the interceptions from last season. It shows how much weight his peers gave everything that followed them.Darnold entered 2025 needing to prove his Minnesota season could travel with him to another offense. He left it holding a Lombardi Trophy.Now, the players who face him have delivered their own verdict: No. 21 in the NFL.
Article Summary: Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold climbed from No. 72 to No. 21 in the player-voted NFL Top 100 after winning Super Bowl LX. NFL players have now placed him ahead of Lamar Jackson, Joe Burrow, Justin Herbert and Dak Prescott.

Article Title: Super Bowl LXI lands on Valentine’s Day for the first time in history creating an unusual football-versus-romance showdown
Article Text:
Super Bowl LXI (Getty Images)

Super Bowl LXI and Valentine’s Day create a unique clash

Super Bowl 2027 brings another major change for NFL fans

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Super Bowl LXI is about to create a very unusual sporting dilemma. The NFL ’s championship game is scheduled for February 14, 2027, putting it on Valentine’s Day for the first time in Super Bowl history. With romance and football competing for the same Sunday, fans have already begun joking about dinner reservations, watch parties and the ultimate relationship compromise.The date alone is enough to make the 2027 Super Bowl stand out. The game will take place at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, on February 14, meaning couples will have to decide how they want to spend one of the biggest nights on the American sporting calendar.For football fans, the answer may seem obvious. For couples with different priorities, however, the evening could require some negotiation.Social media has already embraced the idea. One Reddit commenter joked about the pressure on restaurants, writing:"The Valentine's Day brunch reservations are going to be harder to get than a Super Bowl ticket."Another post took the joke even further, imagining the holiday as a test of romantic loyalty:"Super Bowl on Valentine's? Peak relationship apocalypse incoming—guys choosing touchdowns over touchy-feely dates. Ladies, demand a halftime proposal or it's single season next year."The humor works because the conflict is so easy to imagine. A romantic dinner could overlap with pregame coverage. A reservation might clash with kickoff.And anyone hosting a Super Bowl party could suddenly find themselves planning around Valentine's Day expectations.There is also a convenient escape route. The game falls on Presidents' Day weekend, giving many people the chance to turn the occasion into a longer celebration. Couples could celebrate Valentine's Day on Saturday, watch the Super Bowl on Sunday and use Monday to recover from the late night.The unusual date is not the only reason Super Bowl LXI will be significant. ESPN will broadcast the championship game for the first time in network history, with ABC also carrying the event. ESPN has already outlined extensive programming and storytelling designed to build anticipation well before the game itself.The timing also feeds into a broader conversation about the Super Bowl calendar. The NFL has long faced calls to make the Monday after the championship game a national holiday, particularly because fans already tend to treat Presidents' Day weekend as a natural extension of Super Bowl celebrations.Commissioner Roger Goodell has previously discussed how changes to the NFL schedule could eventually push the Super Bowl toward Presidents' Day weekend. In comments cited in the original report, he said:"I think if you went to 18 weeks regular season that would probably occur," Goodell said at the time. "It is possible somewhere in the calendar. Could happen before that just because of the calendar, the way it lays out.But I think 18 weeks would get you to that point, and I think it would be a really great move."For now, February 14, 2027 remains a one-of-a-kind collision between football and romance. The NFL has confirmed the date, and fans have plenty of time to decide whether Super Bowl Sunday will be a date-night disaster, a couples' tradition or simply the perfect excuse to order wings and watch football together.
Article Summary: Super Bowl LXI is scheduled for February 14, 2027, putting it on Valentine's Day for the first time in Super Bowl history. The game will take place at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, on February 14. The NFL has long faced calls to make the Monday after the championship game a national holiday.
