Brock Lesnar and Ric Flair are two of the biggest names in professional wrestling. But they have had very different experiences in terms of money. Lesnar was a crossover combat-sports star after excelling in amateur wrestling, WWE and the UFC, while Flair made his name over more than four decades in WCW and WWE.But there is a big gap, and public net-worth numbers are best seen as estimates, not audited financial statements. Lesnar’s contracts in the modern era, UFC purses and limited-appearance model allowed him to make individual paydays that were much larger than what was generally available to wrestlers during Flair’s peak years. Meanwhile, Flair continues to earn from his name, appearances, licensing and wrestling-related projects, despite the financial difficulties that have beset his wealth over the years.Brock Lesnar seems to be in a better financial state at the moment. Celebrity Net Worth estimates his net worth at $10 million, whereas NDTV reported an estimate of $17 million in June 2026. Other outlets have published higher numbers, a testament to the uncertainties that come with calculating celebrity net worth.Ric Flair is worth much less. His net worth has been estimated to be $500,000 by Celebrity Net Worth, but other estimates online have put the figure at a much higher number.The variation reflects the absence of publicly verified personal financial records, and the challenge of calculating assets, liabilities, royalties and ongoing income for a longtime entertainer.Lesnar’s wealth is intrinsically tied to his ability to command top dollar. He was an instant star in WWE after debuting in 2002, but he later moved away from the wrestling world to try his hand at the NFL and mixed martial arts before returning to WWE as an established crossover star.Lesnar’s career in WWE has been as much about scarcity as it has been about star power. He was often employed on a limited schedule around major storylines and premium live events for most of his later career instead of working weekly.Lesnar’s UFC career distinguished his money story from most WWE stars. After leaving professional wrestling, he came into MMA and immediately became a big draw. Beating Randy Couture for the heavyweight championship at UFC 91 made him a legit heavyweight champion and gave him a serious bump in commercial appeal.Lesnar has also earned money from endorsements and appearances. Jimmy John’s and other commercial deals are among his previous endorsement deals, and his celebrity status has helped his value outside the ring.He has also kept his lifestyle very private. Recent reports have pointed out that he prefers a rural lifestyle and owning vast amounts of land, rather than the high-profile celebrity lifestyle that many sports stars enjoy.Ric Flair’s financial story started in an era when the economics of professional wrestling were very different. The Nature Boy became one of the defining stars of the National Wrestling Alliance, World Championship Wrestling and WWE, headlining big events and winning championships through a career that spanned several decades.Flair made a ton of money in his time with WCW. One published estimate puts his WCW earnings from 1996-2000 at about $1.95 million. But the size of his earnings did not translate directly into lasting wealth because of taxes, legal obligations, medical expenses and other financial pressures.He also made a lot of money from his WWE career. Flair was a wrestler, manager and personality and stayed a close associate of the company for years. In 2005, during a divorce hearing, it was revealed that his annual WWE salary was reportedly around $500,000, showing how much he could make from wrestling even later in his career.Of the two stars, Flair's financial history is the starkest contrast. Celebrity Net Worth states that in 2000, the IRS filed a lien of more than $870,000 against him, and his further tax problems damaged his finances. The same source reports that in 2019 there was a major medical emergency that resulted in a medical bill of approximately $1.8 million.These pressures help explain why lifetime earnings and current net worth can look so dramatically different. Making millions in a career doesn’t always translate to keeping millions after taxes, debts, medical expenses and other costs.Lesnar’s future financial prospects will probably continue to be linked to his standing as a top-tier combat sports attraction. As his active wrestling career is changing, his name still has value for special appearances, merchandise, licensing and media projects.Flair’s earning model is a unique one. At 77, his money-making opportunities are increasingly linked to his legacy rather than regular ring competition. He still turns up at wrestling events, signs autographs and does other promotional stuff.Lesnar has a path to victory in the modern economics of sports and one of the rare WWE-to-UFC crossover careers. Flair’s financial legacy isn’t so much the wealth he has today, but the incredible value he brought to pro wrestling in terms of sales. Their careers demonstrate two different paths a wrestling superstar can take to earn money: Lesnar with premium modern contracts and crossover sports earnings, and Flair with longevity, character, championships and lasting brand recognition.
Article Summary: Brock Lesnar and Ric Flair are two of the biggest names in professional wrestling. But they have had very different experiences in terms of money. Lesnar was a crossover combat-sports star after excelling in amateur wrestling, WWE and the UFC. Flair made his name over more than four decades in WCW and WWE.

Article Title: “I just want to share that with all these little kids”: How Sophie Cunningham's $10,182 act of kindness turned WNBA frustration into a heartwarming moment for families in need
Article Text:
How Sophie Cunningham's $10,182 act of kindness turned WNBA frustration into a heartwarming moment for families in need(Getty)

Sophie Cunningham turned her WNBA fines joke into a $10,182 act of kindness

Sophie Cunninghum past Ronald McDonald House connection goes back to 2015

Sophie Cunningham had plenty of reasons to be frustrated in 2025. The Indiana Fever guard picked up multiple WNBA fines before a knee injury ended her season early. But a joke she made during that stretch took an unexpected turn. What started as a GoFundMe for fines or even a yacht raised $10,182. Cunningham then chose to give the money to a cause that had already touched her life.On Oct. 2, 2025, Sophie Cunningham launched a GoFundMe with a $26,000 goal. The Indiana Fever guard kept things playful when she explained the reason behind it.“This is more of a joke than anything. For fines only or to charity or for a yacht idk…,” Cunningham wrote on the GoFundMe page.The joke quickly caught on with her supporters. Over the next five days, 171 people donated to the fundraiser. Contributions ranged from $5 to $2,699, and the total eventually reached $10,182.That was when Cunningham decided the money would take a different path. “A yacht would be nice, but whatever we raise here will be going directly to Ronald McDonald House Charities. I’ll take care of my own fines. Y’all are the best,” Cunningham wrote in an update on the GoFundMe page, according to the Indianapolis Star's Oct.10, 2025 report.The decision came after a season in which Cunningham had become increasingly vocal about her frustrations with the WNBA. She had received multiple fines after speaking publicly about league officiating.In an August episode of her podcast, Show Me Something, Sophie Cunningham explained her disciplinary record with a joke of her own.“I’m officially 3-for-3 on being fined by the WNBA,” she said during the episode.She also explained why she continued to speak out, saying, “I promise you, everyone in our league feels that way and I’m just kind of the only one who says something.”So the fundraiser made sense at the moment. Sophie Cunningham had joked about the fines, fans responded and the money started coming in. Yet when she had more than $10,000 sitting in the fundraiser, she did not use it to erase the fines that had inspired the idea.Instead, she picked Ronald McDonald House Charities. That choice also came during a difficult personal stretch. Cunningham's 2025 season ended on Aug. 17 after she tore the MCL in her right knee. She later spent time on the sideline alongside several injured Fever teammates, including Caitlin Clark and Sydney Colson.During the Fever's exit interviews, Cunningham made it clear that she planned to return strong. When reporters asked whether she expected to be healthy for the 2026 season, she answered, “Hell yeah, man,” before saying she hoped to ramp up basketball activities in January.The fundraiser gave Cunningham a chance to do something positive while she waited for her own return.The charity was not just any random act. Sophie Cunningham first encountered Ronald McDonald House Charities as a teenager.Ronald McDonald House Charities helps families stay close to their children while they receive medical treatment. Its programmes provide places to stay, meals and other support for families facing difficult medical situations. Cunningham’s donation therefore went toward a cause that helps families during some of the hardest moments of their lives.On 2015, the Columbia Missourian reported on Cunningham's visit to a Ronald McDonald House in Chicago while she prepared for the McDonald's All-American Game. She met Brian and Jennifer Godish and their four-year-old son, Bradley, who had leukemia. Cunningham played with Bradley, built wooden train tracks with him and joined other children for basketball. She also volunteered to visit children who could not leave the hospital.“It makes me smile because this is how my parents raised me, and I’m just a little bit of who they are. I just want to share that with all these little kids and their parents,” Cunningham told the Columbia Missourian during that 2015 visit.Ten years later, she was once again giving to the same organisation. This time, her fans helped her raise the money.What began as a joke about WNBA fines ended with Sophie Cunningham choosing kindness over keeping the money for herself, adding a meaningful chapter to a connection that started long before her Indiana Fever career.
Article Summary: Sophie Cunningham started a GoFundMe page to raise money for fines or a yacht. The Indiana Fever guard then chose to give the money to Ronald McDonald House Charities. Cunningham first encountered the charity as a teenager during a McDonald's All-American Game.

Article Title: Can Nico Daws become the New Jersey Devils’ No. 1 goalie? Martin Brodeur believes he deserves the chance
Article Text:
Can Nico Daws become the New Jersey Devils’ no. 1 goalie? (Credit: Getty Images)

Why does Martin Brodeur believe Nico Daws deserves a chance?

Nico Daws has already shown the New Jersey Devils what he can do

Can Nico Daws beat Jake Allen and David Rittich for the Devils’ No. 1 goalie spot?

The New Jersey Devils will enter the 2026-27 season without a clear No. 1 goaltender, but Hall-of-Fame goalie Martin Brodeur believes Nico Daws deserves a real chance to take the job. After moving Jacob Markstrom to the Florida Panthers, New Jersey has left the door open for a new starter to emerge.Jake Allen and David Rittich are also in the mix, but Daws could have the biggest opportunity of his young NHL career. Brodeur, who serves as the Devils’ executive vice president of hockey operations, believes the 25-year-old deserves an opportunity to show what he can do in the NHL.According to Brodeur, the Devils are comfortable letting their goaltenders compete for the starting job rather than naming a clear No. 1 before the season begins. “The best starter is going to get the net,” Brodeur told The Hockey News. “I don't think there's a clear-cut No. 1 goalie in net.”That gives Daws a real opening. The 2020 third-round pick has spent much of his career moving between the NHL and AHL, and Brodeur believes the Devils have not given him enough chances to show what he can do.“Nico Daws is a kid who needs a chance,” Brodeur said. “We've been developing him for four years.We didn't put great teams in front of him in Utica and obviously his development slowed down because of that. But we need to give him a chance to see what we have.”While Daws has limited NHL experience, he has already delivered one performance that stands out. In the Stadium Series game against the Philadelphia Flyers at MetLife Stadium, he stopped 51 shots. Brodeur still remembers that performance when discussing Daws’ potential.“We put him into the Stadium Series game at MetLife Stadium in front of 70,000 people and he had 51 saves against the Flyers. He's got it, I really believe in him, we just never gave him a chance,” Brodeur said.That belief could be important for Daws as he competes with Allen and Rittich. Allen brings much more NHL experience, while Rittich has also spent years in the league. But neither has been locked into a heavy workload in recent seasons.Brodeur acknowledged that Markstrom will be missed but believes the current group can give New Jersey what it needs.“Jake showed us a lot last year when he had to play. He played some solid minutes for us,” Brodeur said. “We feel that both goalies are able to play.”If Daws can make the most of his opportunity, he could quickly move from an inexperienced option to the Devils’ top goalie. Brodeur has made his belief clear. Now Daws has the chance to prove it on the ice.
Article Summary: The New Jersey Devils have left the door open for a new No. 1 goalie. Hall-of- Fame goalie Martin Brodeur believes Nico Daws deserves a chance to take the job. Jake Allen and David Rittich are also in the mix, but Daws has the biggest opportunity.

Article Title: Inspiring story on motherhood by Naomi Osaka: “Taking care of myself is part of taking care of my daughter”- Tennis star reveals how self-care changed her approach to parenting
Article Text:
Inspiring story on motherhood by Naomi Osaka: “Taking care of myself is part of taking care of my daughter”- Tennis star reveals how self-care changed her approach to parenting

What did Naomi Osaka mean when she said self-care is part of motherhood ?

How did becoming a mother change Naomi Osaka’s view of tennis?

Why are boundaries so important to Osaka as a mother?

What can mothers learn from Naomi Osaka’s mental-health journey?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For Naomi Osaka, becoming a mother did not mean putting her own needs aside. Instead, it changed the way she thinks about self-care, mental health and life. The four-time Grand Slam champion, who has been open about her struggles with anxiety and pressure, has shared a simple but powerful message: “Taking care of myself is part of taking care of my daughter. ” Her words show why looking after yourself can also be an important part of being a good mother.Osaka became a mother in July 2023 when she welcomed her daughter, Shai, with rapper Cordae. Her journey into motherhood came during a major change in her life. She had stepped away from tennis for more than a year and was also trying to understand what she wanted from her career and her life.For Osaka, self-care is not about putting herself before her daughter. It is about making sure she is in a good place so she can also be there for her child.In her conversations about motherhood and mental health, Osaka has spoken about setting boundaries, taking time for herself and paying attention to what she needs. That can mean taking a quiet moment, meditating, getting enough rest when possible or simply saying no when something feels like too much.Her message also pushes back against the idea that mothers must always put themselves last.Being a mother does not mean a woman has to ignore her own feelings, needs or identity.Osaka’s approach is simple. A mother can love her child deeply and still need time for herself. In fact, taking care of her own mental and emotional health can help her be more present for her child.Tennis had been a huge part of Osaka’s life for years. She became world No. 1 and won four Grand Slam singles titles, including the US Open in 2018 and the Australian Open in 2019, 2021 and 2022.But success also came with pressure. Osaka made headlines in 2021 when she withdrew from the French Open after explaining that media duties were affecting her mental health. She later stepped away from tennis for an extended period.Becoming a mother gave her another chance to look at her life from a different point of view.Osaka returned to professional tennis in January 2024 after giving birth. The comeback was not easy. She had to rebuild her body, return to the demands of professional sport and deal with the normal ups and downs of competition.But motherhood also helped her understand that tennis was only one part of who she was.Winning was still important to her, but it was no longer the only thing that defined her. She could be a tennis player, a mother and her own person at the same time.That change in thinking also helped Osaka become more open about her emotions. Instead of feeling that she always had to appear strong, she became more comfortable talking about difficult moments and asking for support.Osaka has spent much of her career in the public eye. Her matches, interviews and personal life have all received huge attention. That level of attention can be difficult for anyone, and motherhood has given her even more reason to protect her private life and mental space.She has spoken about how hard it once was for her to say no because she worried about disappointing people. Over time, she learned that she could not make everyone happy and did not have to accept every demand placed on her.That lesson became an important part of how she approaches motherhood.For Osaka, boundaries can mean choosing when to work, taking time away from social media, protecting family time or simply refusing to take on something that could leave her overwhelmed.These choices are not about shutting people out. They are about knowing when she needs to step back.Her experience also sends an important message to other mothers. Saying no does not mean you care less. Taking a break does not mean you are lazy. Asking someone for help does not mean you have failed.Sometimes, protecting your own peace is what allows you to give more of yourself to the people you love.Perhaps the biggest lesson from Osaka’s story is that mental health should not be treated as something people have to hide.She has spoken openly about anxiety, pressure and the challenges that came with being a top athlete. She has also talked about wanting her daughter to grow up in an environment where talking about feelings is normal.Osaka has encouraged the idea that children should be able to express themselves, ask for help and understand their emotions. She has also talked about simple habits such as meditation, quiet time and spending meaningful time with family.For her, these lessons are not only things she can tell her daughter. They are things she can show her through her own actions.When a mother rests when she needs to, she shows her child that rest is important. When she talks about her feelings, she shows that emotions are normal. When she asks for help, she teaches her child that nobody has to deal with everything alone.That may be one of the most important parts of Osaka’s message.Motherhood does not have to mean losing yourself. A woman can still have dreams, a career, friendships, personal goals and time for herself while being a loving and devoted mother.Osaka’s journey shows that self-care is not about choosing yourself instead of your child. It is about making sure you are also cared for.For the tennis star, that balance has become part of the mother she wants to be. Her words, “Taking care of myself is part of taking care of my daughter,” capture that idea in the simplest way. Taking care of yourself is not taking love away from your child. Sometimes, it is what helps you give that love with more patience, energy and presence.
Article Summary: Tennis star Naomi Osaka reveals how self-care changed her approach to parenting. Osaka became a mother in July 2023 when she welcomed her daughter, Shai. The four-time Grand Slam champion has been open about her struggles with anxiety and pressure.

Article Title: What’s new in Minecraft? Third Drop 2026 features and more details
Article Text:
Minecraft 26.3 Snapshot 7 has introduced new features (Image via Mojang)

What is the Minecraft Third Drop 2026?

Minecraft Third Drop 2026 features

The Dappled Forest biome

Abandoned Camps

New furniture and building blocks

Mojang is keeping the content pipeline flowing in Minecraft, and the excitement amongst the community is at an all-time high. The next major update is the Third Drop of 2026, and they have yet to reveal the official name for it.It is shaping up to be one of the cosiest and most exploration-friendly updates the game has received in recent memory. It will bring a lot of things, including a brand new biome, a new wood set, furniture blocks, and a brand new structure to discover.Below we have all the details you need to know about the Minecraft Third Drop 2026.The Third Drop 2026 is an upcoming game drop that features dappled forests, abandoned camps, the poplar wood set, wool slabs and stairs, cushions, straw beds, and concrete slabs and stairs.Mojang is testing all the features through the snapshots, and players have already been able to experience most of them.The headline addition of the Third Drop is an entirely new overworld biome. The dappled forest consists of poplar trees with orange, yellow, and red leaves, as well as dirt blocks covered with leaf litter, new red shrubs, and brown mushrooms. After the Chaos Cubed drop took players deep underground, it is a breath of fresh air to have a brand-new destination to discover on the surface.The addition of poplar trees also brings a new wood set, which is a warm grey colour when broken down into planks and slabs. The poplar wood set comes in red, orange, and yellow leaf colors, and poplar saplings can be sold by wandering traders. It is a beautiful addition to the game's palette that builders in particular are going to go absolutely wild for.Scattered through the dappled forest are abandoned camps. They are small structures built from wool stairs and featuring chests or barrels to loot, with a tent-like visual design that fits the woodland explorer fantasy the biome is clearly going for. Having a lootable point of interest in a forest biome gives survival players an actual reason to push into unfamiliar territory.Even better, some abandoned camps contain maps hidden inside their chests. These maps lead to other abandoned camps or various other types of structures in the Overworld, making exploration feel genuinely rewarding in a way that few Minecraft updates have managed before.The drop also brings wool stairs, wool slabs, and wool cushions. Cushions in particular give players a genuine seat block, and pairing them with straw beds gives interiors a soft, homey layer that Minecraft's blocky palette has always struggled to deliver without workarounds.Straw beds are a new bed variant that lets players sleep through the night without changing their spawn point. They can only be used once and will be destroyed after use, and cannot be used in the Nether or the End. It is an elegant solution for players who want to skip the night on long expeditions without permanently shifting their respawn location.Concrete slabs and stairs have also been added as part of the final batch of features from the third drop, rounding out a building-focused update that is sure to keep the community's creative side busy for months to come.
Article Summary: The Third Drop 2026 is an upcoming game drop that features dappled forests, abandoned camps, the poplar wood set, wool slabs, cushions, straw beds, and concrete slabs and stairs. Mojang is testing all the features through the snapshots, and players have already been able to experience most of them.

Article Title: Inspiring story of the day: “She’s my everything. I love her” How Tom Brady’s mother Galynn defied cancer and stood by the star QB through adversity and his historic Super Bowl comeback
Article Text:
How Tom Brady’s mother Galynn defied cancer and stood by the star QB through adversity and his historic Super Bowl comeback(Getty)

How Galynn Brady ’s cancer diagnosis changed the family’s 2016 season

How Tom Brady supported his mother while facing his own adversity

How Galynn Brady fought through treatment with one goal in mind

How Super Bowl LI became Galynn Brady victory too

Why Robert Kraft gave Galynn Brady her own Super Bowl ring

How Galynn Brady recovery brought another reason for Tom Brady’s family to celebrate

How Galynn’s strength became part of Tom Brady’s story

Success stories are often remembered through championships and records, but Tom Brady’s 2016 season also came with a difficult time for his family. While Brady served a four-game suspension, his mother, Galynn, was undergoing treatment for stage 2 breast cancer, including chemotherapy and radiation.Unable to attend his regular-season games, Galynn watched from home before making it to Super Bowl LI , where she watched Brady lead the Patriots back from 28-3 to beat Atlanta 34-28. After the victory, Brady said, “She’s my everything. I just love her so much.” Tom Brady's mother, Galynn's cancer battle began in the summer of 2016. In an interview with NFL correspondent Andrea Kremer, she remembered sitting in a doctor's office when she was told that she had breast cancer. Doctors told her it was stage 2, but she also learned that the cancer was fast-growing and aggressive.“I just remember sitting in the doctor’s office and them telling me ‘You have breast cancer. It’s only stage 2,’” Galynn recalled. “And so the journey began.”That journey involved five months of chemotherapy, followed by radiation and other treatment. The diagnosis immediately changed the family's routine because Galynn had traditionally been a regular presence at Tom's games.During the 2016 season, however, her health prevented her from travelling to Patriots games.Instead, football became something she watched from home while concentrating on treatment. Her husband, Tom Brady Sr., later explained how the family structured its weeks around Galynn's chemotherapy and Tom's games.“Everything centered around 10 o'clock Thursday morning” for her chemotherapy and then Sunday morning when the family would watch football, he explained. Even while dealing with cancer, Galynn continued following her son's season. Those Sunday games gave the family a familiar routine during months that were anything but normal.Galynn's illness was not the only major challenge facing the Brady family that season. Tom entered 2016 dealing with the fallout from the Deflategate controversy and a four-game suspension.For Brady, watching his mother go through cancer treatment while also dealing with his own public struggles was emotionally difficult. Years later, while discussing that period in Man in the Arena, he explained how painful it had been for Galynn to see her son publicly criticised.“I think, personally, that was very difficult for her to see her son kind of raked through the coals like I was,” Brady said.He believed his mother had already been carrying the stress of her own illness, so seeing what was happening to her son added another burden. The family therefore became an important source of support for both Galynn and Tom.During his suspension, Brady spent time with his family at Pebble Beach in California. His ex wife Gisele Bündchen, daughter Vivian, nieces and nephews were also there. Brady later recalled standing on the 18th hole and looking around at the people closest to him while thinking about what really mattered.“Being with my family at a very vulnerable time,” he said, gave him a different perspective.Instead of allowing football to consume every part of his life, Brady recognised that his mother's health and his family's well-being deserved his attention too.As the Patriots' season continued and the team moved closer to another Super Bowl appearance, the Brady family began thinking about whether Galynn would be healthy enough to attend.Tom Brady told his parents that she would be ready for the Super Bowl. According to Tom Brady Sr., the family had calculated that the end of Galynn's five months of chemotherapy would fall about two weeks before the championship game.Galynn completed her final round of chemotherapy on January 12, 2017. But her recovery did not immediately become easy. She developed pneumonia and shingles, leaving her ability to travel to Houston in doubt.Her doctor did not clear her for the trip until one day before the family was scheduled to leave.Galynn could have stayed home after everything she had endured, but she wanted to see her son play.“There’s a special bond between a mother and a son,” Galynn said. “I just wanted to be there for Tommy, and I wanted to be there with our family. Everybody was going to the Super Bowl and I didn’t want to miss that.”Those words explain why reaching Houston meant so much to her. She had spent months watching Tom from home while going through chemotherapy, but she wanted to be beside him and her family when the Patriots reached the biggest game of the season.Her determination also showed how she approached the cancer battle itself. She was not allowing the illness to completely take away the moments she valued most.Galynn finally made it to Houston, but the game itself quickly became another test for the family.The Patriots fell behind the Atlanta Falcons 28-3, leaving New England with a massive deficit to overcome. Galynn watched from the stands as the team struggled, and the situation became so painful that she eventually told her husband she wanted to leave.“I said to Tom, ‘I just want to go home,’” she later recalled. “I was heartbroken for Tommy.”Tom, however, continued fighting. The Patriots gradually erased the deficit and eventually forced overtime. New England completed the comeback with a 34-28 victory, giving Brady his fifth Super Bowl championship and the Patriots the largest comeback in Super Bowl history.For Galynn, the emotion was overwhelming after everything she had experienced.“I’m so glad that I decided I would go and just put cancer aside for that weekend,” she later said. She had made it to Houston despite the complications that had threatened her recovery, and she was there to watch her son produce one of the most remarkable comebacks in NFL history.The Patriots' victory gave the Brady family a moment they would never forget, but Robert Kraft added another deeply personal gesture afterward. The Patriots owner gave Galynn her own Super Bowl ring, recognising her connection to the team's unforgettable championship season. Kraft's gesture acknowledged what she had endured while Tom was leading New England toward the title.For Galynn, the ring represented much more than the Patriots' victory. It was connected to the months of chemotherapy, the health complications, the uncertainty over whether she could travel and the decision to put her illness aside long enough to be there for her son.The Super Bowl did not mark the end of Galynn's recovery, but it was an important milestone. In June 2017, Tom Brady Sr. said that Galynn had finished her cancer treatment about two months earlier and was doing well, playing golf and tennis again.In August, Tom Brady gave another encouraging update, saying his mother was “on the road to recovery” after receiving very positive test results. “She’s doing really well,” Brady said. “Everyone in our family is so happy.”By October, reports said Galynn's latest cancer screening had come back clear, although her cancer carried a high risk of recurrence. She continued to undergo regular testing as part of her follow-up care.Her experience also encouraged her to share a message with other people facing cancer. Galynn said she hoped people could learn from her story and keep a positive attitude rather than giving up hope.“I would hope that they would learn to keep a positive attitude, and not to give up hope,” she said. “Be thankful every day; think about the people that are caring about you.”That is perhaps the most directly inspirational message from Galynn herself, because it came from someone who had actually gone through the treatment she was describing.Galynn had supported Tom long before he became one of the most successful quarterbacks in NFL history. She was there throughout his career and remained one of the people closest to him, but her cancer battle showed just how strong their bond had become.In 2016, both mother and son were facing challenges that demanded patience and resilience. Tom had to deal with suspension and the pressure surrounding his career, while Galynn had to endure chemotherapy, radiation and serious health complications.Neither could simply remove the other's struggle, but they continued encouraging each other.Tom's support was important to Galynn during treatment, especially when she struggled with the physical changes brought by chemotherapy. She later recalled losing her hair and wearing a bandanna, while Tom would reassure her by telling her she looked beautiful.Galynn, meanwhile, gave Tom another reason to keep pushing when the Patriots faced their biggest challenge of the season.Her decision to travel to Houston brought their two journeys together. She had fought through cancer treatment to be there, and Tom responded with one of the greatest performances of his career.That is what makes Galynn Brady's story so powerful. She was not simply watching her son play football while recovering from cancer. She was actively fighting her own battle, trying to stay positive and refusing to let the illness take away the moments she wanted to share with her family. Tom Brady's Super Bowl LI comeback will always be remembered for the 28-3 deficit, the overtime victory and another championship for one of the NFL's greatest quarterbacks.For the Brady family, however, the night carried a much deeper meaning.Galynn had fought through cancer to sit in those stands. Tom had fought through his own adversity to lead the Patriots back. When the two finally embraced after the victory, the moment represented everything they had endured together.
Article Summary: Tom Brady's mother, Galynn, was diagnosed with breast cancer in the summer of 2016. She underwent five months of chemotherapy, followed by radiation and other treatment. Brady watched from home before making it to Super Bowl LI, where she watched Brady lead the Patriots back from 28-3 to beat Atlanta.

Dallas Mavericks forward PJ Washington has landed in trade rumors as San Antonio looks for a deadline addition to complement its NBA Finals roster. The Spurs are largely running things back after last season's run, but a fix at power forward is already looking necessary if Tobias Harris keeps struggling to find his footing in the rotation.Washington just started a four-year, $88.7 million deal, and Dallas now has Cooper Flagg on the roster and a fresh extension for Naji Marshall on the books. That combination has created a frontcourt crowd the Mavericks may want to thin out. There is now talk that Washington and Harris could be the centerpiece of a swap that solves a problem on each side.Washington has settled into a role as one of Dallas's most versatile defenders, someone who can guard multiple positions and knock down open looks when the offense finds him. That fit mattered most in 2024, when the Mavericks acquired him at the trade deadline after a Grant Williams signing fell short, then rode his three-and-D game all the way to the NBA Finals.Two years later, the roster around him looks different. Cooper Flagg's arrival and a new extension for Naji Marshall have stacked Dallas's forward group, and Washington's name has started showing up in trade speculation as a result.San Antonio brought in Tobias Harris on a two-year deal specifically to fill its power forward spot, but according to insider Tyler Watts, the fit has not settled the way the Spurs hoped. Watts wrote that Harris "wouldn't be the first veteran that couldn't find a fit on a new roster," and flagged him as a name San Antonio could move if the situation does not improve.Washington's defensive range and outside shooting are exactly what a title-hopeful Spurs team wants next to a still-developing Victor Wembanyama, especially with the Knicks and Thunder both shedding money this offseason instead of adding pieces. San Antonio has the draft capital to make a deal work even though Harris's expiring money alone would not match Washington's contract.On Dallas's end, moving Washington clears a logjam that Flagg's arrival and Marshall's extension created, giving the Mavericks a shorter-term contract and future draft compensation instead of a long-term deal at a position they no longer need to fill.Washington gives the Spurs a forward who can guard multiple positions and space the floor around Wembanyama, which is closer to what San Antonio wanted from the power forward spot when it signed Harris in the first place. With the Knicks and Thunder both standing pat to manage their own cap situations, San Antonio has a real chance to be the team that makes a move before Wembanyama's next contract number changes the math.Harris arrives on an expiring, shorter contract, giving Dallas more flexibility than Washington's four-year deal offered, and the attached draft compensation gives the Mavericks a longer-term asset instead of another proven veteran at a position already crowded by Flagg and Marshall. It is not a direct value swap in Dallas's favor, but it addresses the roster fit question the brief raises.Washington fills an immediate need next to Wembanyama at a position the Spurs already tried and failed to solve with Harris, while Dallas is banking more on future draft value than on-court production in return.

Washington's defensive range and outside shooting are exactly what a title-hopeful Spurs team wants next to a still-developing Victor Wembanyama.

Article Title: How a doctor's 'amazing ACL' verdict on Michael Penix Jr. could completely change the Falcons' quarterback plans this season
Article Text:

What did Michael Penix Jr.'s doctor say about his ACL?

Does the ACL news affect the Falcons' QB competition with Tua Tagovailoa?

Michael Penix Jr. hasn't taken an 11-on-11 rep at Falcons training camp yet. His shot at the Week 1 starting job is likely gone, with Tua Tagovailoa set to open the season under center in Atlanta. But on Wednesday, Penix dropped a piece of news that reframed the entire conversation around his future. His doctor, after examining the reconstructed ACL in Penix's left knee, offered a verdict that almost no one recovers from three tears expecting to hear.Speaking to reporters at the Falcons' Flowery Branch facility, Michael Penix Jr. shared a direct quote from his physician that caught a lot of people off guard. "This is an amazing ACL. You should never have any more knee problems for the rest of your career."That's a remarkable thing to say about a player who has now torn the same ligament three times. Penix suffered his most recent ACL tear in November during the 2025 season and went under the knife shortly after. The standard nine-to-twelve-month recovery window put Week 1 clearance in serious doubt from the start. Eight months in, the doubt has hardened into near-certainty -- Tua starts, Penix waits.But the doctor's assessment changes the long-term read on Penix entirely. Prior to this, the natural concern was whether a third ACL reconstruction would leave him vulnerable to re-injury, or worse, force a premature end to a career that's barely had a chance to start at the NFL level.Instead, the medical staff appears to be saying the opposite: the repair is clean, strong, and built to last.Penix has been careful with his words throughout camp, avoiding percentages and exact timelines. "I'm not really chasing a timeline. I'm just chasing trying to be better every day," he said earlier this week. His doctor's report, though, suggests the patience is paying off in ways that go beyond this season.In the short term, not really. Tua Tagovailoa has been running first-team reps, and the Falcons named him Atlanta's preseason starter. Penix hasn't been cleared for full team drills, and with four weeks still possibly remaining before he advances to the next stage of his recovery, there's simply no realistic path to him winning the job before the opener.The bigger picture is more interesting. Penix has been throwing well in 7-on-7 sessions and has told reporters his body feels strong. He's hitting weight targets and taking his diet seriously. None of that is fluff -- it's a guy methodically putting himself in position to take over the moment the door opens.If Tua struggles or gets hurt, Atlanta will turn to Penix without much hesitation. He's the player they selected in the first round. He's the one the organization built around before Kirk Cousins was cut loose and Tagovailoa was brought in as a bridge. The Falcons aren't abandoning that investment -- they're just buying time.Now, with a doctor saying his knee is built to hold up for the rest of his career, the Penix story has shifted from injury concern to opportunity. He just has to stay ready.
Article Summary: Michael Penix Jr. has torn the same knee ligament three times. His shot at the Week 1 starting job is likely gone, with Tua Tagovailoa set to open the season under center. Penix hasn't been cleared for full team drills, and there's no realistic path to him winning the job before the opener.
